rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial intensifier for saying something is damn or extremely so.
Use this for a stronger, more dramatic emphasis, especially before an adjective or verb.

example.english: I chased the bus damn hard.
example.jyutping: ngo5 sei2 gam3 zeoi1 baan1 ce1

rows.note: Use this casual intensifier when the meaning is roughly really or damn, especially with energetic or impressive descriptions.

example.jyutping: nei5 paau2 dak1 ging6 faai3 wo3

rows.note: Use 死 as a blunt intensifier before a negative adjective or noun, as in 死蠢 for “damn stupid.”

example.english: You’re damn stupid; you don’t even know how to open a door.
example.traditional: 你死蠢㗎，連門都唔識開。
example.jyutping: nei5 sei2 ceon2 gaa3 lin4 mun4 dou1 m4 sik1 hoi1

rows.note: Use 鬼咁 for broad emphatic degree, especially when “damn” means “very” rather than a swear word.

example.english: It’s damn hot today, so remember to bring water.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 gwai2 gam2 jit6 gei3 dak1 daai3 seoi2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual exclamation for irritation, anger, or surprise.

example.english: Damn, there’s a hole in my trousers!
example.jyutping: ding2 tiu4 fu3 cyun1 zo2 go3 lung1

rows.note: Use this when something has gone wrong or you suddenly realize a problem.

example.english: Damn, I forgot to bring my keys.
example.jyutping: bai6 laa3 ngo5 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 so2 si4

rows.note: Use this for alarm, dismay, or an exasperated “oh no” reaction.

example.english: Damn, the document hasn’t been saved!
example.jyutping: sei2 laa3 fan6 man4 gin2 mei6 jau5 bou2 cyun4
